requirements.text: The TCU shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
The TCU shall carry the international approval mark described in paragraph 5.3 on every unit conforming to the approved type.
The TCU shall have its approval mark affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form.
The TCU approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
The TCU approval mark shall show the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle.
The TCU shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, complies with the requirements of UN R10.
The TCU shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The TCU shall not exceed 62 to 52 dBµV/m broadband radiated emissions in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically above 30 MHz.
The TCU shall not exceed 52 to 63 dBµV/m broadband radiated emissions in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically above 75 MHz.
The TCU shall not exceed a constant 63 dBµV/m broadband radiated emission limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
The TCU shall show measured broadband radiated emission values below the type approval limits.
The TCU shall not exceed 52 to 42 dBµV/m narrowband radiated emissions in the 30 to 75 MHz band, decreasing logarithmically above 30 MHz.
The TCU shall not exceed 42 to 53 dBµV/m narrowband radiated emissions in the 75 to 400 MHz band, increasing logarithmically above 75 MHz.
The TCU shall not exceed a constant 53 dBµV/m narrowband radiated emission limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
The TCU shall show measured narrowband radiated emission values below the type approval limits.
The TCU shall withstand, over 90 per cent of the 20 MHz to 2 GHz band, 60 V/m stripline, 75 V/m TEM cell, 60 mA BCI, 30 V/m ALSE or 21 V/m reverberation chamber, depending on the method applied.
The TCU shall withstand, over 90 per cent of the 2 to 6 GHz band, 10 V/m in ALSE or 7 V/m in a reverberation chamber, depending on the method applied.
The TCU shall withstand, over the whole 20 MHz to 2 GHz band, a minimum of 50 V/m stripline, 62.5 V/m TEM cell, 50 mA BCI, 25 V/m ALSE or 18 V/m reverberation chamber.
The TCU shall withstand, over the whole 2 to 6 GHz band, a minimum of 8 V/m in ALSE or 6 V/m in a reverberation chamber.
The TCU shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity related functions during the radiated immunity tests of Annex 9.
The TCU shall be tested for conducted transient immunity on its 12 V supply lines using the starting profile of ISO 16750-2 and ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.
The TCU shall meet functional status B when related to immunity related functions and status D otherwise for the starting profile, with 10 pulses for a 12 V system.
The TCU shall meet functional performance status III for test pulse 1 at -75 V on a 12 V system over 500 pulses.
The TCU shall meet functional performance status I for immunity related functions and III otherwise for test pulse 2a at +37 V over 500 pulses.
The TCU shall meet functional performance status II for immunity related functions and III otherwise for test pulse 2b at +10 V over 10 pulses.
The TCU shall meet functional performance status I for immunity related functions and III otherwise for test pulse 3a at -112 V for 1 hour.
The TCU shall meet functional performance status I for immunity related functions and III otherwise for test pulse 3b at +75 V for 1 hour.
The TCU, where it is not switched and contains no switches or inductive load, is exempt from the transient conducted emission test of paragraph 6.7.
The TCU's cellular RF transmitter shall be tested in transmit mode, with wanted emissions within the necessary bandwidth and out-of-band emissions disregarded.
The TCU shall keep spurious emissions within the limits of this Regulation.
The TCU shall be manufactured so that production-sample emission levels do not exceed the reference limits by more than 4 dB.
The TCU shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity related functions up to the conducted disturbance levels of paragraph 6.9.1 in production verification.
The TCU's cyber security approval mark, where affixed, shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The TCU shall implement proportionate mitigations protecting the vehicle type against the risks identified in the risk assessment.
The TCU shall implement measures to detect and prevent cyber-attacks against the vehicle.
The TCU shall provide data forensic capability enabling analysis of attempted or successful cyber-attacks.
The TCU's cryptographic modules used for cyber security shall be in line with consensus standards.
The TCU shall verify the authenticity and integrity of every message it receives over its external and in-vehicle communication channels.
The TCU shall implement security controls for storing cryptographic keys, such as a hardware security module.
The TCU shall apply access control techniques and designs to protect its system data and code from unauthorised manipulation, overwrite or erasure.
The TCU shall protect confidential data transmitted to or from the vehicle.
The TCU shall employ measures to detect and recover from denial of service attacks on its communication channels and internal network.
The TCU shall employ measures to prevent and detect unauthorised access, including attempts to gain privileged access.
The TCU, acting as gateway, shall implement measures to detect malicious internal CAN/Ethernet messages.
The TCU shall employ secure over-the-air software update procedures.
The TCU, as a system with remote access, shall apply security controls protecting its remotely operable functions.
The TCU shall apply security controls to its external interfaces, including the vehicle diagnostic interface and any exposed ports.
The TCU shall be developed following cyber security best practices for software and hardware, removing development remainders such as debug or JTAG ports.
The TCU shall undergo cyber security testing with adequate coverage to verify the effectiveness of the implemented security measures.
The TCU shall protect the authenticity and integrity of OTA software updates to prevent their compromise and invalid updates.
The TCU shall make each RXSWIN it holds uniquely identifiable.
The TCU shall make each RXSWIN or declared software version easily readable via a standardized electronic communication interface, at least through the OBD port.
The TCU shall protect the RXSWINs and software versions it stores against unauthorised modification.
The TCU shall restore target ECUs to their previous software version, or place the vehicle into a safe state, after a failed or interrupted update.
The TCU shall only execute a software update when the vehicle has enough power to complete the update, including any recovery or safe-state transition.
Where an update may affect vehicle safety, the TCU shall use technical means ensuring the vehicle is in a state in which the update can be executed safely.
The TCU shall inform the vehicle user, before execution, of the update's purpose, functional changes, expected duration, unavailable functionalities and necessary instructions.
Where executing the update while driving is unsafe, the TCU shall ensure the vehicle cannot be driven during execution of the update.
Where executing the update while driving is unsafe, the TCU shall disable the vehicle functionalities that would affect vehicle safety or the successful execution of the update.
The TCU shall inform the vehicle user of the success or failure of an executed update.
The TCU shall inform the vehicle user about the changes implemented by the update and any related updates to the user manual.
The TCU shall ensure defined preconditions are met before executing a software update.
